about: Fishing villages and towns on the Coast Lab map, with SOURCED phases for the lab's year slider (1700-2025). Written by hand from fetched pages; nothing here comes from memory.

confidenceKey.high: a museum, heritage-agency or municipality page states the year
confidenceKey.medium: sv.wikipedia or a tourism page states the year
confidenceKey.low: a decade or century only, years borrowed from the regional period, population-table reading, or the page flags its own claim as unsourced. An entry carries its weakest fact.

phaseRule: At a given year the phase that covers it is shown; if several cover it, the one with the latest "from" wins. "to": null means no end year is stated (shown through 2025). A place is hidden before firstRecorded; with firstRecorded null it is drawn at every year as an outlined marker. Years with no phase show as plain "settled" (a display default, not data).

herringPeriods.note: Regional periods for all of Bohuslän; per-place phases above copy these years only where a source about that place says it took part.

list.label: the great herring period
variants: 1747-1808: vastsverige.com Uddevalla page, sv.wikipedia Marstrand, Rörö

settlements.name: Smögen
settlements.firstRecordedNote: "Första gången Smögen nämndes i litteraturen var 1594" (vastsverige.com)

phases.note: Hotell Smögens Hafvsbad completed 1900; summer guests came for seaweed baths. End of the resort phase not stated.

notes: Granite quarrying "tog fart under 1800-talets slut" (century only, left out).

settlements.name: Kungshamn
settlements.firstRecordedNote: no year found in the sources read

phases.note: Place page: the great herring period of the 1700s gave permanent settlement. Years are the regional period.
Abba's whole production moved to Rösholmen in 1943 (Munkens cannery was there earlier, year not stated); moved to Hagaberg, Kungshamn, in the early 1970s.

notes: Name appears on a sea chart "från tidigt 1600-tal" (no year). A 1933 sale to Bröderne Ameln was NOT confirmed on the page and is left out.

settlements.name: Lysekil
settlements.firstRecordedNote: Name form "Lusekijll" 1578 (page sentence paraphrased by the fetch tool). The 1317 form "Lysa" refers to the church village.

phases.note: Population peaked at 536 in 1770 and fell to 391 in 1820.
"Under 1800-talets senare hälft utvecklades Lysekil till en badort." Second half of the 1800s only; no exact years.

notes: Herring periods 1566-1587 and 1666-1675 are before the slider starts. Town rights 1 April 1903 are administrative, left out.

settlements.name: Gullholmen
settlements.firstRecordedNote: no year found in the sources read

phases.note: Place page: salting works, cannery and sailmaker arrived during the great herring periods of the 1700s and 1800s. Years are the regional period.
As above (second period).
Population table: 811 in 1910, 466 in 1950, 85 in 2015. "Decline" is read from the numbers, not stated by the page.

notes: First mention "under senare delen av 1500-talet" (no year).

settlements.name: Klädesholmen
settlements.firstRecordedNote: "På holländska kartor från 1594 kallades ön Cleefsholmen"

phases.note: "under den stora sillperioden 1747–1809" (place page).
"Under 1808 försvann sillen." Population just over 400 by 1830 (end year not re-checked).
"sillen kom in till kusten på nytt 1877–1900" (place page).
"omkring 1950 fanns det 25 konservfabriker"; since 1970 only herring pickling. Snapshot years, not start and end dates.

settlements.name: Marstrand
settlements.firstRecordedNote: "Namnet Marstrand finns belagt från 1293"

phases.note: Place page: the herring period that began in 1747 ended in 1808.
Place page lists 1878-1898, flagged "källa behövs" (citation needed) on the page itself.
The first "badhus" was created in 1822; one of the country's early spa resorts. End year not stated.

notes: Free port 15 Aug 1775 to 15 May 1794: not tied to herring on the page, so not a phase.

settlements.name: Rörö
settlements.firstRecordedNote: no year found in the sources read

phases.note: A salting works and train-oil works stood on the islet Rammen east of Rörö during the great herring period, 1747-1808 (place page).
By 1824 the whole installation on Rammen had been dismantled.
